correctness.rationale: This is the supremum over all SPD orientations at a fixed condition number and all nonzero gradients, not a bound attained for every fixed Hessian. In units where eigenvalues lie in [1,κ], use the gradient-squared spectral weights, with moments m1 and m2. Exact line search gives α=1/m1, h=g⁺ perpendicular to g, and ||h||₂²/||g||₂²=m2/m1²−1. The inequality m2≤(1+κ)m1−κ yields the sharp Euclidean factor c=(κ−1)/(2√κ) by maximizing at m1=2κ/(1+κ). Projection onto g's perpendicular space bounds |h_j| by c times (Σ_{i≠j}g_i²)^{1/2}. The supplied two-plane block has trace 1+κ, determinant κ and sends the chosen unit g=u to a step with h=cv; its projections attain the claimed factor. Equivalently take any sharp Euclidean step and rotate to g supported equally on n−1 coordinates, h supported on the remaining coordinate. For κ=1 the update is zero. Solving c√(n−1)≤1 yields the stated inclusive threshold. Independently checked the displayed 3×3 matrix by exact symbolic arithmetic: spectrum {1,1,4}, α=5/8, h=(3√2/4,−3√2/8,−3√2/8), which gives both ratios. The frozen decimal checker was read, not run.

evidence: Theorem 4.1 gives the Euclidean squared ratio bound (κ−1)²/(4κ) for every steepest descent step on a strictly convex quadratic; its equation (4.3) reduces the inequality to Kantorovich in z=A^{1/2}g.

Kantorovich equality in this specific expression is realized with z proportional to e_min+e_max: at A=diag(1,κ) the product of the two Rayleigh factors is (1+κ)²/(4κ). Identity extension realizes any dimension n≥2. Equation (4) of the exact-line-search analysis gives h⊥g.
